S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).

subtypes.Animal Type: Marked fear of animals or insects like dogs, bees, snakes, or spiders.
subtypes.Natural Environment Type: Marked fear of the natural environment like storms, heights, water, or the dark.
subtypes.Blood-Injection-Injury Type: Marked fear of seeing blood, receiving injections, or medical procedures.
subtypes.Situational Type: Marked fear of specific situations like airplanes, elevators, tunnels, bridges, or enclosed spaces.
subtypes.Other Type: Marked fear of other situations like choking, vomiting, loud sounds, or costumed characters.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Anticipatory Anxiety: Strong anxiety triggered just by thinking about the possibility of encountering the phobic object.
subtypes.Immediate Panic Response: Overwhelming fear erupting immediately upon facing the phobic object.
subtypes.Physiological Panic Symptoms: Intense physical reactions such as heart palpitations, shortness of breath, sweating, or trembling.
subtypes.Freezing: Feeling paralyzed or unable to move due to extreme fear.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Active Avoidance: Intentionally and completely staying away from contact with the phobic object or situation.
subtypes.Functional Impairment due to Avoidance: Accepting severe restrictions on daily life, job, or social activities to avoid the phobic object.
subtypes.Enduring with Distress: Forcing oneself to endure the situation while experiencing intense fear and anxiety because it cannot be avoided.
subtypes.Reliance on Safety Signals: Barely enduring the exposure by relying on a companion or safety object.

symptom.disease_info: Specific Phobia is characterized by a marked, persistent fear of a specific object or situation that reliably triggers immediate fear or anxiety and leads to avoidance or enduring the situation with intense distress. The fear is out of proportion to the actual danger, typically lasts at least 6 months, and causes functional impairment; it is distinguished from agoraphobia, social anxiety disorder, and panic disorder by its circumscribed focus on a particular object or situation.

patient.stressor: When Oliver moved from a low, familiar shared house in Durham to a fifth-floor apartment closer to his training job, the building’s old elevator became part of his daily routine. At first he simply preferred the stairs after a brief elevator malfunction, but over the next 7 months he came to treat elevators as far more dangerous than the situation warranted, feeling immediate fear whenever he had to enter one and increasingly planning his workdays, volunteer visits, and photography outings around avoiding them. The impairment remained limited but real: he declined a workshop assignment in a Boston high-rise and stopped visiting one senior computer student who lived in an elevator-only building. He eventually contacted his employer’s assistance program himself after realizing his careful scheduling had become organized around avoiding elevators rather than around his actual responsibilities.

S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).
S062.manifestation: I know an elevator in an office block is probably safe, but when I look at those old doors in my apartment building or at work, my mind treats it like I’m about to get trapped or dropped, even though part of me knows that sounds over the top.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.
S063.manifestation: As soon as I step toward an elevator or hear it clunk open, my chest tightens, my hands get sweaty, and I feel this rush of panic before I’ve even had time to think it through.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.
S064.manifestation: I’m here because I’ve started planning my days around not using elevators—taking five flights of stairs at home, turning down a workshop in a high-rise, and even stopping visits with one of my older computer students because his building doesn’t really have another option.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: It has started affecting my work and volunteering because I turned down a high-rise workshop assignment and stopped visiting a senior computer student whose building basically requires the elevator.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about 7 months, since shortly after I moved into the fifth-floor apartment and had that elevator scare.
